title: Tibetan nuns
hookLine: nunneries rebuilding, and in recent years the first nuns awarded the highest study degree

lines: WOMEN IN MAROON, AT THE FRONT.
cards: A row of women with shaved heads and maroon robes stands at the front of a hall. Their teachers are there, and their families, and other nuns who crowded in to watch.
One by one, the women step forward to receive a degree, a white scarf, applause. Behind each of them sit years of memorizing, studying and arguing over the same great texts that monks study.
The degree has a name: geshema. For a long time it existed only in its other form, geshe, held by monks. Now there are nuns who hold it.

teach.b: Tibet has had nuns and nunneries for a long time, often smaller and poorer than the great monasteries, and with less access to the full course of philosophical study. Then came upheaval.
Nunneries in Tibet were destroyed or emptied. In exile, in India and Nepal, nuns built again, often from almost nothing: a few rooms, a teacher, a kitchen. Inside Tibet, nunneries were rebuilt too.
In exile, some nunneries made a deliberate choice.

teach.h: THE SAME TEXTS AS THE MONKS.
teach.b: Their nuns would study the same curriculum as the monks: the Perfection of Wisdom, the Middle Way, logic, the monastic rules. And they would debate it, in their own courtyards, with the same sharp questions.
For years it was slow work, finding teachers and building the texts into their days.

In recent years, nuns from these programs sat the final examinations, and the geshema degree was awarded: the same top level of study that monks reach with the geshe. Senior lamas publicly supported the step.
Tibetan tradition gives nuns the novice ordination, but the lineage of full ordination for women did not take root in Tibet, and how to restore it is still discussed among Tibetan teachers.
Some Tibetan nuns have received full ordination in other Buddhist lineages. Different teachers hold different views, and the conversation continues.
Meanwhile, in the courtyards, the clapping goes on, and women are doing it.

how: Tibetan Buddhist nuns live in nunneries in Tibet, India, Nepal and elsewhere; in some nunneries they follow the full philosophical curriculum, including courtyard debate, and some have been awarded the geshema degree.

games.q: you lead a small nunnery in exile, with a few rooms and one teacher. what do you choose for your nuns' education?
o: prayers only, since the full course is for monks.
the same full curriculum the monks study, debate included.
games.why: some nunneries chose the full curriculum. it was slow, hard work, and it led, in recent years, to the geshema degree.

practice: Bring to mind a woman whose knowledge you have leaned on: a teacher, an author, a doctor, a grandmother who knew the name of every plant.
Ask what she had to learn, and how long it took her, to know it that well, and name one thing she knows that you still use. If you'd like, say her name once, out loud.

wordCard.voice: Tibetan nuns. Women who rebuilt their nunneries, took up the full course of study, and in recent years earned the geshema degree. Today's word.

orig.note: Tibetan dge bshes ma: geshe with the feminine ending ma. The degree as held by nuns.

carryVoice: Your line: they study too. The same texts, the same sharp questions. I'll be here tomorrow.
